candidates.question: A data-flow review compares GitHub.com pull request text completion with an on-demand pull request summary. Which description identifies the contextual inputs documented for text completion, rather than substituting the summary's diff-based prompt workflow?

answerChoices.text: File diffs are assembled to request an overall summary of the changes.
PR title, existing prose, commit titles, partial diffs and recently viewed titles inform continuation.
Code near the cursor and snippets from open tabs form an editor prompt.
The active shell and previous conversation turns supplement a terminal user's request.

candidates.explanation: Text completion uses the pull request's title, existing text and other contextual material to continue the description. Requested summaries have a separately described diff-based workflow.
candidates.deepExplanation: The comparison concerns input construction, not permissions, availability or a guarantee that every possible change is represented. The two features should not inherit each other's undocumented limits.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: This describes the separate on-demand summary workflow named in the stem.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.c: This describes IDE inline code suggestions, not GitHub.com description completion.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.d: This describes Windows Terminal context, not pull request description completion.

answerChoices.text: Pull request titles, existing descriptions and partial code diffs.
Selected code changes for a commit summary and description.
Cursor-adjacent code and snippets from other open editor tabs.
The active shell's name and the current chat history.

candidates.explanation: For Windows Terminal, the card identifies the active shell and chat history as context combined with the prompt.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: Those inputs describe commit-message generation rather than terminal Chat.

candidates.question: A Copilot Chat deployment already uses a supported BYOK provider. Its architecture diagram includes the provider's model but omits GitHub from the response path before presentation. Which documented behavior requires correcting that omission?

answerChoices.text: Responses still pass through GitHub's API and may undergo content filtering.
The selected model supplies the main agent-mode conversation.
The provider's API key is configured for the chosen provider.
Open-file and repository information can supplement the user's input.

candidates.explanation: BYOK responses still pass through GitHub's API. Content filtering may occur before display; choosing a provider does not remove this documented response path.
candidates.deepExplanation: This does not assert that filtering is always active or sufficient, nor that GitHub performs every specialized action through the chosen provider. It identifies one explicit response-path component.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: This identifies the primary model but not the omitted GitHub response step.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.c: Credential configuration does not explain the omitted response-path component.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.d: Input enrichment does not identify the downstream response-path component.
